## About this page

What is open and what is folded away when you add or edit an item, and whether new logins start with a password.

#### How it works

The editor keeps an item's main fields on show and puts the rest in sections you can open, such as websites, the one-time code and notes. **Sections open at the start** chooses which of them start open. **Behavior** decides whether your own opening and closing changes that, and what else the editor does for you.

#### On Android

What is shown and open when you add or edit an item, whether new logins start with a password, and which card reader to use.

The editor shows the fields a kind of item needs, and one **Add more** line for the rest. **Shown and open at the start** chooses which sections are there from the start, open. **Behavior** decides whether your own opening and closing changes that, and what else the editor does for you.

See also [Item editor](/guide/screens/#screen-editor), [Add menu](/guide/settings/add/), [Generator](/guide/settings/generator/).

<a id="setting-editor-open"></a>

## Sections open at the start

Which sections of the editor are open when it starts. The others show as one line that opens when you choose it.

#### How it works

Most sections also open by themselves when they already hold something, so a saved website or note is never out of sight.

- Websites and apps, for logins.
- One-time code, for logins and codes.
- Notes, for every type except a note.
- More fields, for fields you name yourself.
- Security questions, for logins.
- Organize, for the folder, tags, icon, color and favorite.
- More details, for a type's less used fields, when [Fold less used fields](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-fold-details) is on.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Shown and open at the start.

Which sections of the editor are on show, and open, when it starts. The rest wait behind one **Add more** line.

A section that already holds something is always shown, but it starts folded like the rest, its line saying what is inside, unless its switch here is on. One you add under **Add more** opens straight away. Websites and apps, Other details and Organize are always shown, so their switches only open them.

- Websites and apps, for logins.
- One-time code, for logins and codes.
- Notes, for every type except a note.
- Custom fields, for fields you name yourself.
- Security questions, for logins.
- Organize, for the folder, tags, icon, color and favorite.
- Other details, for a type's less used fields, when [Fold less used fields](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-fold-details) is on.

See also [Remember what I open](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-remember), [Fold less used fields](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-fold-details).

<a id="setting-editor-remember"></a>

## Remember what I open

Opening or closing an empty section in the editor changes its switch under **Sections open at the start**, so it starts the same way next time.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | The editor learns from what you open and close. |
| Off | The switches stay as you set them here, whatever you do in the editor. |

#### On Android

Opening or closing a section in the editor changes its switch under **Shown and open at the start**, so it starts the same way next time.

See also [Sections open at the start](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-open).

<a id="setting-editor-fold-details"></a>

## Fold less used fields

Keeps a type's everyday fields on show and puts the rest under **More details**, such as a card's PIN or a database's connection string.

#### How it works

Cards, identities, SSH keys, API keys, databases, licenses, recovery items and Wi-Fi networks have fields to fold. Logins, notes, codes and documents show all of theirs.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Those types show their everyday fields first, with **More details** below. It opens by itself when one of its fields has something in it. |
| Off | Every field of the type shows at once. |

#### On Android

Keeps a type's everyday fields on show and puts the rest under **Other details**, such as a card's PIN or a database's connection string.

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Those types show their everyday fields first, with **Other details** below. It starts folded, its line naming the fields inside, unless its switch under **Shown and open at the start** is on. |
| Off | Every field of the type shows at once. |

See also [Sections open at the start](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-editor-open), [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds).

<a id="setting-editor-generate"></a>

## Start logins with a password

Fills in a generated password every time you start a new login.

#### How it works

The password follows your [generator settings](/guide/settings/generator/): its type, length and characters. A login started from the generator with **Save as login** keeps the value you made there.

#### When to use it

Turn it on if you mostly add logins for new accounts. When you save a password you already have, you will type or paste over the generated one.

#### Limits

It also fills the first password field of other new items that have one: a database, a Wi-Fi network, or an SSH key's passphrase.

See also [Generator](/guide/settings/generator/), [Type](/guide/settings/generator/#setting-gen-mode), [Generated passwords](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-generator).

<a id="setting-auto-tag"></a>

## Tag new items

Gives a new item the tag its site suggests, such as Banking or Social, when you save it without tags of your own.

#### How it works

The tag comes from WM Pass's list of known sites, or from an item's name when that is a known site's, such as PyPI. The offline model's guesses do not tag a new item. An item you tag yourself keeps only your tags. One added while a tag's list is open still gets its site's tag, beside that one.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | A new item saved with no tags of your own gets its site's tag. |
| Off | A new item has only the tags you give it. |

#### Limits

It applies when an item is first saved. Items already in the vault are left as they are.

#### On Android

The tag comes from WM Pass's list of known sites, or from an item's name when that is a known site's, such as PyPI. The offline model's guesses tag only with [Use guesses too](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-auto-tag-guess) on. An item you tag yourself keeps only your tags.

It applies when an item is first saved. [Add suggested tags](/guide/settings/editor/#action-bulk-tags) does the same for items already in the vault.

See also [Item editor](/guide/screens/#screen-editor), [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds).

<a id="setting-auto-tag-guess"></a>

## Use guesses too

*Only in Android.*

Lets [Tag new items](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-auto-tag) tag a new item from the offline model's guess when no list knows its site.

#### How it works

The model reads the item's name and address on this phone and answers only when it is fairly sure. It is still wrong more often than the list.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | A new item whose site is not on the list gets the model's guess. |
| Off | Only the site list and known names tag a new item. |

See also [Tag new items](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-auto-tag), [Add suggested tags](/guide/settings/editor/#action-bulk-tags).

<a id="action-bulk-tags"></a>

## Add suggested tags

*Only in Android.*

Tags the items already in your vault in one go, after you look through what would be added.

#### How it works

Each suggestion says where it came from, and you pick which sources count:

- *Site list*: the site is on WM Pass's list of known sites. On to start with.
- *Item's name*: the name is a known site's, such as PyPI. On to start with.
- *Kind*: what the item is, such as Payment cards or SSH keys. Off to start with.
- *Guesses*: the offline model's best guess from the name. Off to start with.

Suggestions are grouped by tag. Open a group to leave out any item, or clear its box to leave out the whole tag. **Only items with no tags yet** skips anything you have tagged already.

The button at the foot, such as **Add 3 tags to 2 items**, tags what is left, and the message after it offers **Undo**, which takes every one of those tags back off.

See also [Tag new items](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-auto-tag), [Use guesses too](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-auto-tag-guess).

<a id="setting-card-reader"></a>

## Reader

*Only in Android.*

Which reader the camera uses when you scan a payment card into a card item.

#### How it works

Both readers work on this phone, from the camera picture. The first scan asks which one to use, and this is where you change your answer.

- *Google (ML Kit)* reads the expiry date and the name too. WM Pass's own reader runs beside it on the same pictures, because ML Kit reads general text and often misreads the raised or foil digits of a card number that the built-in reader was trained on; the number comes from whichever is sure first. Google's library sends Google statistics about how it runs, with details of the phone and app, and Play services fetches it the first time, so the first scan may use WM Pass's own reader alone.
- *WM Pass* is built in, from Stripe's open card scanner, and sends nothing to anyone. It reads the card number only, so you type the expiry date and the name.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Ask next time | The next scan asks which reader to use. |
| Google (ML Kit) | Reads the number with WM Pass's own reader alongside, and the expiry date and name. Google gets statistics about how the library runs. |
| WM Pass | Reads the number only, and sends nothing. |

#### Limits

Only builds that include Google's libraries offer the choice. Other builds always use WM Pass's own reader. This setting is not carried in a settings file, so someone else's file cannot pick the reader that talks to Google.

See also [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds), [Item editor](/guide/screens/#screen-editor).
